Counsel for Applicant :- Ajeet Kumar
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Jaspreet Singh,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned AGA for the State-respondent.

By means of the instant bail application, the applicant seeks bail in respect of FIR/Case Crime No.358/2023, under Sections 406, 420, 467, 468, 471, 504, 409, 120B IPC, Police Station Zaidpur,
District Barabanki.

The submission of the learned counsel for the applicant is that as per the averments made in the FIR, it is alleged by the complainant that certain documents were got signed by the applicant and the other co-accused in order to provide some job to the complainant.
However, the said documents Aman Verma vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

It is only when the bank officials approached the complainant for recovery of the said loan, at that stage, he become aware and it was realized that the complainant has been duped.
It was stated that the applicant had not taken any loan and he had not opened any account and the entire transaction is fraudulent.
The submission of the learned counsel for the applicant is that the applicant is working as Branch Manager of Bank of India, Barauli Branch, District Barabanki.
It is further urged that insofar as the bank transaction is concerned, this loan related to a Government Scheme known as Mudra Loan.

In the said Scheme, it is not cash which is advanced rather any item which is required to be purchased is made available and the seller is paid the amount directly from the bank for which no separate guarantor is required.

In the aforesaid backdrop, it is submitted that this in itself could not have been done by the applicant inasmuch as under his scope of work, the applicant is only required to verify the fact given by the person applying for the loan.

The only requirement as called for by the applicant is to verify the details and in the aforesaid circumstances merely because the form upon which the loan was applied did not have full information or it did not have the signature of certain officials does not indicate any complicity insofar as the applicant is concerned.
The facts verified by the applicant are also required to be re-verified at different level and only then the said loan could have been processed.
Merely by blaming the applicant, it cannot be said the applicant had any role to play.

It is also stated that the applicant has explained his criminal history and in Para-31 of the bail application wherein eight number of cases have been mentioned, it would reveal that all related to similar transaction where the applicant has been roped in falsely.

In the aforesaid circumstances where the applicant has a stable house hold, there is no apprehension that the applicant is at flight risk and in a position to influence any witness or tamper with the evidence coupled with the fact that the applicant is languishing in jail since 08.10.2023.
It is, therefore, prayed that the applicant be enlarged on bail.

Learned A.G.A., on the basis of material in the case diary available with him, has opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that upon the verification of the documents there were certain shortcomings at the behest of the applicant which is also verified from the statement of the other witnesses and in such circumstances, it cannot be said that the applicant does not have any role and for the said reason, the bail application deserves to be rejected.

Considering the rival submissions as well as considering the facts and circumstances, it is at a premature to say whether mere lapses on the part of the applicant would be sufficient enough to charge him.
The fact that the loan is processed and it goes through different layers of scrutiny is not disputed by the State.

Also noticing that the applicant is in jail since 08.10.2023 as well as considering the nature of allegations and accusation against the applicant, the severity of the Aman Verma vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

2 punishment if convicted and the period of incarceration as well as the fact that no apprehension has been expressed by the learned AGA that the applicant is at the risk of fleeing justice or that he would tamper with evidence or influence any witness
, hence, at this stage, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, this Court is of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.

Let the applicant Aman Verma involved in the aforesaid FIR/Case Crime Number be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond with two reliable sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned.
At the time of executing required sureties the following conditions shall be imposed in the interest of justice.
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.

In case of default of this condition,
it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i)
opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.
If in the opinion of the trial court, absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause,
then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Order Date :- 14.5.2024 Rakesh/-
